thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: streaming-tail.p99 has breached SLO in eu-west2. Auto-escalation: paging on-call.
maya: getting paged — looking into p99 tails on streaming reads. Graphs show a sharp jump starting ~3951234200. p95 also rising but p99 is worse.
liam: I see increased TLS handshake times from our ingress NAT path (eu-west2-a -> eu-west2-b). Packet retransmits up. Could be cross-AZ egress congestion.
oscar: Confirming, tcp_retransmits per-conn up by ~300% on nat-gw-eu-3. BPF captures show SYN->SYN-ACK delays and some duplicate acks.
maya: customer impact: heartbeat timeouts for streaming clients ~10-30s. Some short-lived sessions dropping. CC has flagged a handful of paying customers seeing degraded UX.
netbot: Observed DNS retries in same window — resolver failures gone from 0.1% to 2.4% for eu-west2. Correlated with NAT ephemeral port exhaustion alerts from infra.
oncall-junior: Running quick checks now: `kubectl get pods -n runtime | grep streaming` — no obvious pod restarts. Connections look healthy on host side.
liam: Can we try rerouting egress for a small subset to nat-gw-eu-4 which has spare ephemeral capacity? Suggest adding a policy to steer 10% traffic.
oscar: +1. Also recommend enabling aggressive TCP keepalives for streaming proxy to reduce half-open TTLs while we investigate.
maya: Doing staged reroute: applying policy to route 10% of streaming traffic to nat-gw-eu-4 now. Will watch p99 in 1m.
incident-bot: Runbook step triggered: streaming-tail-triage -> Check NAT ephemeral ports and route split. `sre-runbook-bot` queued.
sre-runbook-bot: Suggested commands:
```
# show ephemeral usage
aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=nat-gw-eu-* --query '*[].{eni:NetworkInterfaceId,ephemerals:Attachment}'
# tcpdump on suspect host
sudo tcpdump -nni any "tcp and port 443" -c 200 -w /tmp/handshake.pcap
```
oscar: tcpdump shows many retransmits and some ICMP unreachable from internal router toward nat-gw-eu-3. Could be intermittent path MTU or queue drops.
gwen: paging networking infra on-call (cc @netops) — any recent routing changes or maintenance in eu-west2?
netops (via netbot): No planned maintenance. We see a short-lived BGP flap at 3951234178 between az-b and az-c lasting ~30s — likely noisy link.
liam: That lines up with the start of the spike. Hypothesis: transient inter-AZ link packet loss caused connection stalls, clients retried DNS, NAT state churn increased ephemeral collisions and handshake retries -> p99 jump.
maya: Early mitigation summary:
- We split egress traffic 90/10 to nat-gw-eu-4 (rolled back to 80/20 after observation)
- Enabled aggressive TCP keepalives on streaming proxies
- Increased ephemeral port range on nat-gw-eu-3 to reduce exhaustion risk
- Temporary route preference to avoid known noisy BGP path
Effect: p99 dropped from ~9.2s to ~1.8s over 6 minutes. p95 back to normal.
oncall-junior: Noted a residual 250ms tail on a subset of tenants — digging into per-tenant routing to see if any still hitting the old path.
gwen: CS notified for interim customer update. Flagging top 5 affected customers for SRE follow-up.
liam: Follow-up items:
- Net team to run sustained BGP and interface diagnostics on az-b <-> az-c link
- Infra to check NAT gateway autoscaling/port table logic (why ephemeral spike correlated so tightly)
- Runtime to add more robust telemetry for per-connection egress path so we can triage faster next time
maya: Handing off to oncall-junior for monitoring and postmortem notes. If anything regresses, page paging rota immediately.
oncall-junior: Taking handoff — will monitor 15m and collect logs/pcap for postmortem. Leaving the reroute in place for 20m then will re-evaluate.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident mitigated to degraded-normal. Please update incident tracker with notes and start a retrospective ticket if root cause confirmed.
maya: Adding short TL;DR for tracker: transient inter-AZ link packet loss -> increased TCP retransmits -> DNS retries + NAT ephemeral pressure -> streaming p99 spike. Mitigations: route split, ephemeral tunables, tcp keepalives. Follow-ups assigned.
oscar: Attaching local pcap summary to ticket: `/var/log/pcaps/3951234321-handshake.pcap` (internal path)
oncall-junior: marking resolved on-call handoff. Leaving watch for 30m then will close thread. :thumbsup:
